title: Microsoft 365 Backup: activity logs for policy and restore operations
summary: The briefing remains supported by the current Microsoft documentation and supplied records. The changed What's new page still gives the same activity-log date, workloads, retention and access rules; the briefing correctly distinguishes operational activity logs from Microsoft Purview Audit.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start> -EndDate <end> -Operations BackupPolicyActivated searches the specified Backup audit operation.

claims.claim: The activity-log view is inside Microsoft 365 Backup and concerns use of that service.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup Activity Logs provide an in-product view of backup policy and restore operations. ... Open Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.claim: Learn's activity-log section lists required roles but no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Backup" "activity logs" "license" "charge". Read the full Activity logs section of backup-privacy-security: its Required roles list names Global, Backup, SharePoint and Exchange administrators and names no licence.

claims.claim: The Backup overview says billing is consumption-based rather than traditional user-based licensing.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup is a pay-as-you-go offering that charges based on consumption, unlike traditional user-based licenses.

claims.claim: The overview billing table labels the $0.15 rate per GB per month, unlike the pricing page's GiB label.
claims.quote: **Billing model** ... $0.15 per GB per month for all data protected by Backup

claims.claim: Purview retains audit records for 180 days for users with other non-E5 Office 365 or Microsoft 365 licences without the named audit add-ons.
claims.quote: For users assigned any other (non-E5) Office 365 or Microsoft 365 license, the system retains audit records for 180 days.

claims.claim: Purview retains Entra ID, Exchange and SharePoint audit records for one year by default for E5 users or users with Purview Suite or the E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on.
claims.quote: For users assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license (or users with a Microsoft Purview Suite ... or Microsoft 365 E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license), the system retains audit records for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, and SharePoint activity for one year by default.

claims.claim: The Purview audit activities table lists BackupPolicyActivated for Microsoft 365 Backup.
claims.quote: | Activated a Backup Policy | BackupPolicyActivated | A Microsoft 365 Backup policy is activated from an inactive state. |

claims.claim: The Purview audit activities table lists RestoreTaskCompleted for Microsoft 365 Backup.
claims.quote: | Completed Restore Task | RestoreTaskCompleted | A restore task is completed in Microsoft 365 Backup. |

claims.claim: Activity-log viewing permissions depend on assigned administrator roles.
claims.quote: Role-based access controls will apply. Administrators will only be able to view logs for workloads they are authorized to manage.

claims.claim: The activity-logs page does not provide its own access-granting control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Backup" "activity logs" "enable" "permissions". Read backup-privacy-security and backup-setup. Access is described through administrator roles; the logs page documents filters, search and export, not role assignment or an access-granting control.

claims.claim: Learn does not state the behaviour when the activity-log system reaches 1 million activities.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Backup" "activity logs" "million" "earlier". Read backup-privacy-security and the activity-log entry in backup-whats-new; both state the capacity but neither explains behaviour at the limit.

claims.claim: Learn does not state whether activity history preceding the mid-October 2026 rollout appears.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Backup" "activity logs" "million" "earlier". Read backup-privacy-security and backup-whats-new; neither states whether pre-rollout activity history appears. The supplied notice likewise gives no historical-backfill rule.

claims.claim: No date for moving the Graph activityLogs endpoint to v1.0 is documented in the checked references.
claims.quote: Searched: "backupRestore/activityLogs" "v1.0". Read List activityLogs and returned activityLogBase and restoreTaskActivityLog excerpts; they identify beta and its production limitation but give no date for a v1.0 release.

claims.claim: MC1489931 says Microsoft will update the notice with documentation.
claims.quote: We will update this post with new documentation.

claims.claim: The notice recommends informing backup administrators that activity monitoring will be available directly within the product.
claims.quote: We recommend that you inform your backup administrators that activity monitoring for Microsoft 365 Backup will be available directly within the product.
